# VoxShift

> VoxShift is a free, open-source AI voice changer for Windows, macOS and Linux that changes your voice in real time (~30 ms) and sends it to Discord, OBS, Twitch, Zoom and games through a virtual microphone.

VoxShift re-synthesizes your voice with an RVC-class neural model instead of only shifting pitch, so breaths, emotion and accent are preserved. Typical end-to-end latency is 25–35 ms on an NVIDIA RTX, AMD RX 6000 or Apple M1 GPU and 45–60 ms in Low-CPU mode. A live latency meter shows the exact number.

It is for gamers, streamers, VTubers, VRChat users, podcasters and content creators. The setup wizard installs a signed "VoxShift Virtual Mic" driver; you select it as the input device in Discord, OBS, Zoom, Teams, Steam, TeamSpeak, VRChat or a game. No Voicemeeter or cable routing is needed.

Everything runs locally, including voice cloning in Voice Lab. There is no account, no telemetry and no ads, and offline mode blocks every network call.

VoxShift does not touch any game process; to the system and to games it is a standard audio input device, like a USB microphone. It is not meant for impersonating real people without consent, fraud, harassment or bypassing voice-based authentication.

## Key facts

- Price: free; no paid tiers, ads, watermarks or time limits
- License: MIT (open source)
- Platforms: Windows 10/11 (x64, ARM64), macOS 12+ (Apple Silicon and Intel), Linux x86_64 (AppImage, .deb, Flatpak)
- Install: installer .exe, portable .zip, winget `VoxShift.VoxShift`, Scoop, Homebrew cask `voxshift`, Flathub `app.voxshift.VoxShift`
- Offline/privacy: fully offline capable; no account, no telemetry; voice cloning never uploads audio
- GPU: optional; CUDA, DirectML (AMD/Intel), Apple Metal or CPU
- Minimum: 4-core CPU (2015+), 4 GB RAM, no GPU (Low-CPU mode)
- Recommended: 6+ cores, NVIDIA GTX 1660 / RTX 20xx+, AMD RX 6000+ or Apple M1+, 8 GB+ RAM
- Voice Lab training: 6 GB+ VRAM (NVIDIA) or Apple M-series
- Version: 1.0.0; releases are signed and ship with SHA-256 checksums
- Built with: Rust audio engine, Tauri 2, React, ONNX Runtime, PyTorch (Voice Lab)

## Features

- Real-time AI voice conversion with a live latency meter and A/B blend of original and AI voice
- Voice Lab: train a custom voice model locally from about 10 minutes of audio; export `.pth` / `.onnx`
- 250+ free AI voices (anime girl, demon, robot, ghost, narrator, monster, ASMR and more)
- Import any RVC v1/v2 `.pth` or `.onnx` model; community voices in the Voice Hub
- Soundboard with global hotkeys that work in full-screen games; any key can switch voices
- Virtual microphone driver for any app with a microphone input
- AI noise and echo suppression before conversion
- Voice-to-file converter for MP3, WAV, FLAC, MP4, MKV and MOV (video stream kept intact)
- Text-to-speech with any voice and emotion
- Low-CPU mode with under 10% CPU usage on laptops and older PCs
- WASAPI / ASIO low-latency audio settings

## Common questions

- Is VoxShift really free? — Yes. It is MIT-licensed with no paid tiers, ads, watermarks or time limits.
- How do I change my voice on Discord for free? — Install VoxShift, pick a voice, click Voice ON, then set Discord's input device to "VoxShift Virtual Mic" in Voice & Video settings.
- How much latency does it have? — Typically 25–35 ms on a mid-range GPU and 45–60 ms in Low-CPU mode.
- Can I clone my own voice locally? — Yes. Voice Lab trains a model from about 10 minutes of your audio entirely on your PC; nothing is uploaded.
- Does VoxShift work without a GPU? — Yes. Low-CPU mode runs lightweight models on any modern 4-core CPU.
- Will a voice changer get me banned in Valorant, CS2 or Fortnite? — VoxShift does not touch the game process; it is a standard audio input device, like a USB microphone.
- Can I use RVC models from the internet? — Yes. Import RVC v1/v2 `.pth` or `.onnx` models via Voice Library → Import; respect each model's licence.
- Does it work on macOS and Linux? — Yes. macOS 12+ uses Metal on Apple Silicon; Linux uses a PipeWire / PulseAudio virtual source.
- Is VoxShift a Voicemod alternative? — Yes. It covers real-time voices, soundboard, hotkeys and a virtual mic, and adds local voice cloning, file conversion and TTS, free and without an account.
- Can it change the voice in a video file? — Yes. Converter & TTS replaces only the voice track in MP4, MKV or MOV and keeps the original video.

## Alternatives it is compared with

- Voicemod, Clownfish, MorphVOX Pro, Voice.ai (comparison table in the README)
